title: WSL Proxy Relay settings
description: The settings in appsettings.json next to WSLProxyRelay.exe, and in the user's %LOCALAPPDATA%\WSLProxy\settings.json, which is layered on top.

Relay.description: The relay: its port, the upstream proxy, the bypass list and its limits.

ListenPort.description: The TCP port the relay listens on, on 127.0.0.1 only.

Upstream.description: The upstream proxy that requests not matched by the bypass list go to. When its host is empty, every request goes direct.

Host.description: The upstream proxy's host name or IPv4 address. Empty means no upstream.

HealthCheckIntervalSeconds.description: How often to probe the upstream proxy with a TCP connect, in seconds. 0 turns probing off.

NoProxy.description: Destinations that bypass the upstream proxy and go direct, one entry per item: * on its own for everything, example.com or .example.com for the name and its subdomains, *.example.com for subdomains only, an IPv4 address, or an IPv4 CIDR range such as 10.0.0.0/8. Every form but a CIDR range can end in :port. Keep the default in appsettings.json empty, because configuration merges arrays by index.

DenyLocalDestinations.description: Refuses loopback, link-local, unspecified, multicast and broadcast destinations, and localhost names, with 403.

Limits.description: Size and time limits that protect the relay from misbehaving peers.

MaxRequestLineBytes.description: The longest request line accepted. Longer gets 414. At most MaxHeaderBytes.

MaxHeaderBytes.description: The largest request or response head accepted, request line included. Larger gets 431, or 502 for a response.

MaxHeaderCount.description: The most header fields accepted in one head. More gets 431, or 502 for a response.

HeaderTimeoutSeconds.description: How long a client has to send a complete request head once it starts one, in seconds.

ConnectTimeoutSeconds.description: How long to wait for a TCP connection to a destination or the upstream proxy, in seconds.

IdleTimeoutSeconds.description: How long a keep-alive connection may sit idle between requests, or a response may stall, in seconds.

TunnelIdleTimeoutSeconds.description: How long a CONNECT tunnel may carry no bytes in either direction before it's closed, in seconds.

MaxConnections.description: The most client connections open at once. More are refused with 503.

StartAtLogin.description: Starts the app when the user signs in to Windows.

LogRetentionDays.description: How many days of log files to keep. Read at start-up.

LogWindowLines.description: How many recent log lines the log window keeps in memory. The log files keep everything. Read at start-up.

Logging.description: Log levels for the log files and the log window.

LogLevel.description: The lowest level logged, by category prefix, such as WSLProxy or Microsoft. Default applies to every other category.
